regional_scope: Minnesota / Upper Midwest (Prairies, open woods, shorelines across Minnesota)

regional_scope: Minnesota / Upper Midwest (Woodland edges, pastures, open valleys)

regional_scope: Minnesota / Upper Midwest (Acidic northern Minnesota pine/oak forest floors)

regional_scope: Minnesota / Upper Midwest (Cool northern Minnesota mossy spruce-fir woods)

regional_scope: Minnesota / Upper Midwest (Rich shaded southern/southeastern Minnesota deciduous woods)
voucher_source: Bell Museum Herbarium and USDA PLANTS

regional_scope: Minnesota / Upper Midwest (Woodlands, edges, floodplains, and bogs across Minnesota)
voucher_source: Bell Museum Herbarium and USDA PLANTS

poisonous_lookalike: Menispermum canadense, Rhamnus cathartica, Actaea pachypoda/rubra, Taxus, Solanum, Phytolacca

accepted_binomial: Quercus alba / Quercus macrocarpa / Quercus rubra
regional_scope: Minnesota / Upper Midwest (Oak savannas and hardwood forests across Minnesota)
voucher_source: Bell Museum Herbarium and USDA PLANTS

regional_scope: Minnesota / Upper Midwest (Woodland understories, oak savannas, edges)
voucher_source: Bell Museum Herbarium and USDA PLANTS

observable_exclusions: Tree-nut anaphylaxis risk (hazelnut/birch-pollen cross-reactivity); bristly irritating hairs on beaked-hazelnut husks; moldy kernels

regional_scope: Minnesota / Upper Midwest (Southern/southeastern Minnesota rich river valleys & woods)

poisonous_lookalike: Aesculus (opposite palmate leaves, toxic buckeyes), Carya (hickory — solid non-chambered pith, 4-valve splitting husk)
observable_exclusions: Tree-nut anaphylaxis; juglone hull sap causes persistent skin staining/dermatitis; moldy fallen hulls harbor tremorgenic mycotoxins dangerous to dogs and people

regional_scope: Minnesota / Upper Midwest (Rich slopes and valleys in eastern/southeastern Minnesota)
voucher_source: Bell Museum Herbarium and USDA PLANTS

diagnostic_features: Closely related to black walnut with lighter ridged gray bark, dark chocolate chambered pith, velvety pad above leaf scars, and elongated lemon-shaped sticky fuzzy husks enclosing jagged nuts
poisonous_lookalike: Juglans nigra (round green husks, lacking velvety upper leaf-scar pad)
observable_exclusions: Butternut is severely threatened by lethal butternut canker fungus and is a Minnesota Species of Special Concern—DO NOT harvest or damage native butternut trees

regional_scope: Minnesota / Upper Midwest (Southeastern & central Minnesota hardwood forests)
voucher_source: Bell Museum Herbarium and USDA PLANTS
diagnostic_features: Alternate pinnately compound leaves (5 large leaflets with peeling curved bark plates in shagbark; 7–9 leaflets with bright sulfur-yellow naked buds in bitternut); four-part husks splitting along sutures around smooth angled nuts
poisonous_lookalike: Juglans (chambered pith, non-splitting husk), Aesculus (opposite leaves, toxic buckeye)
observable_exclusions: Opposite palmate leaves (buckeye); intensely bitter unpalatable tannins in bitternut; tree-nut allergy; moldy fallen kernels

regional_scope: Minnesota / Upper Midwest (Eastern Great Lakes vs Minnesota native range)

observable_exclusions: Out-of-range field-guide plates mislead travelers into misidentifying ornamental or toxic planted trees (e.g., horsechestnut/buckeye) as native forest nuts

regional_scope: Minnesota / Upper Midwest (Shallow northern Minnesota lakes and slow rivers)
voucher_source: Bell Museum Herbarium and USDA PLANTS

poisonous_lookalike: Phragmites, Phalaris (reed canary grass), Zizaniopsis

regional_scope: Minnesota / Upper Midwest (Minnesota prairies, meadows, open slopes)
voucher_source: Bell Museum Herbarium and USDA PLANTS

poisonous_lookalike: Silphium (cup plant/compass plant), Rudbeckia, toxic Packera/Senecio or contaminated farm-edge crops

synonyms: Conifer cone scales vs toxic buckeyes
regional_scope: Minnesota / Upper Midwest (Minnesota forests and planted parks/edges)

poisonous_lookalike: Aesculus glabra (Ohio buckeye) and Aesculus hippocastanum (horsechestnut) — contain esculin glycosides and saponins causing vomiting, stupor, paralysis, and pediatric fatality
observable_exclusions: Treat ALL smooth shiny eye-spotted buckeyes and horsechestnuts as strictly poisonous; never roast or handle crushed husks near food

synonyms: Spoilage and allergy gate for wild nuts/seeds
regional_scope: Minnesota / Upper Midwest (All fallen nut and seed collection contexts)
voucher_source: Bell Museum Herbarium and USDA PLANTS
diagnostic_features: Rejects any wild nut or seed showing shell cracks, dark discoloration, musty odor, fuzzy mold, shriveled bitter meat, or insect tunnels because Aspergillus and Penicillium molds produce carcinogenic/neurotoxic mycotoxins
poisonous_lookalike: Moldy black-walnut hulls, damp ground acorns, rotten hickory/hazelnut kernels, toxic Aesculus
observable_exclusions: Tree-nut and seed anaphylaxis can be rapidly fatal even from trace exposure; heat does NOT destroy established aflatoxins

regional_scope: Minnesota / Upper Midwest (Freshwater marshes, ponds, slow waters across Minnesota)
voucher_source: Bell Museum Herbarium and USDA PLANTS
diagnostic_features: Tall spongy thick leaves rounded on back (D-shaped cross-section) sheathing tightly around a round stem; unmistakable dense cylindrical brown flower spike
poisonous_lookalike: Iris versicolor (toxic blue flag iris — flat sword leaves folded in a tight 2-ranked flat fan, showy blue-violet iris blooms, toxic iridin rhizomes), Sparganium, Acorus
observable_exclusions: Flat overlapping fan-like leaf bases; missing brown flower spike; polluted stormwater ditches; public wetland digging bans

regional_scope: Minnesota / Upper Midwest (Shallow clean freshwater marshes and river backwaters)
voucher_source: Bell Museum Herbarium and USDA PLANTS
diagnostic_features: Long-stalked distinct arrowhead-shaped leaves with pointed basal lobes; whorls of three-petaled white radial flowers; underwater starchy tubers
poisonous_lookalike: Calla palustris (toxic wild calla — heart-shaped leaves, white hood spathe), Peltandra virginica (arrow arum — green spathe, severe calcium-oxalate needle toxins)
observable_exclusions: Hooded spathe-and-spadix arum flowers (severe oral-burning calcium oxalates); polluted wetlands; public-land wetland digging prohibitions

regional_scope: Minnesota / Upper Midwest (Rich Minnesota hardwood slopes & open meadows)
voucher_source: Bell Museum Herbarium and USDA PLANTS

observable_exclusions: ANY bulb or strap-leaf plant lacking immediate strong onion/garlic odor on both leaf and bulb triggers instant STOP; wild leeks take 5–7 years to mature and digging is prohibited in parks/SNAs

regional_scope: Minnesota / Upper Midwest (Moist edges, river bottoms, sunny roadsides across Minnesota)
voucher_source: Bell Museum Herbarium and USDA PLANTS

poisonous_lookalike: Toxic non-sunflower roots if dug after tops die back; contaminated roadside or agricultural ditches
observable_exclusions: Missing intact flowering/fruiting sunflower stems; public-land digging bans; inulin fiber causes intense GI cramping in many people

regional_scope: Minnesota / Upper Midwest (Moist woodland edges, stream banks in southern/central MN)
voucher_source: Bell Museum Herbarium and USDA PLANTS

regional_scope: Minnesota / Upper Midwest (Native dry tallgrass prairies of western Minnesota)

regional_scope: Minnesota / Upper Midwest (Minnesota woodlands, thickets, and river edges)
voucher_source: Bell Museum Herbarium and USDA PLANTS

diagnostic_features: Climbing vines (black-bristled woody stem in S. tamnoides; thornless herbaceous stem in S. herbacea) with alternate smooth-edged heart/oval leaves featuring 3–7 strong parallel curving veins and paired tendrils arising from the petiole base

observable_exclusions: Vines lacking paired tendrils and parallel arched leaf veins (moonseed/nightshade); hard woody rhizomes not dug on public lands

regional_scope: Minnesota / Upper Midwest (Minnesota lakes, slow rivers, and protected aquatic beds)
voucher_source: Bell Museum Herbarium and USDA PLANTS

observable_exclusions: Pulling aquatic plants in Minnesota public waters violates DNR aquatic-plant protection laws; alkaloids and lake-sediment heavy metals make raw rhizomes hazardous

regional_scope: Minnesota / Upper Midwest (Rich moist deciduous woods in spring)
voucher_source: Bell Museum Herbarium and USDA PLANTS

diagnostic_features: Delicate spring ephemeral with one pair of opposite narrow grass-like stem leaves beneath a loose cluster of five-petaled white flowers delicately striped with pink veins
poisonous_lookalike: Erythronium, Dicentra (toxic Dutchman breeches — finely dissected ferny foliage, alkaloid-rich corms)
observable_exclusions: Dissected fern-like leaves (Dicentra); public parks and SNAs prohibit digging delicate woodland spring ephemerals

regional_scope: Minnesota / Upper Midwest (Fields, roadsides, open edges across Minnesota)
voucher_source: Bell Museum Herbarium and USDA PLANTS

diagnostic_features: Demonstrates extreme morphological overlap inside Apiaceae: wild carrot has bristly hairy green stems, a tiny purple central floret, and three-forked lacy bracts beneath the umbel—yet shares habitats with lethal smooth purple-spotted Conium maculatum (poison hemlock) and wetland Cicuta maculata (water hemlock)
poisonous_lookalike: Conium maculatum (poison hemlock — lethal coniine paralysis), Cicuta maculata (spotted water hemlock — lethal cicutoxin seizures), Pastinaca sativa (wild parsnip burns)
observable_exclusions: BECAUSE TINY IDENTIFICATION ERRORS IN APIACEAE ARE RAPIDLY FATAL, THIS ENCYCLOPEDIA ENFORCES AN UNCONDITIONAL STOP ON WILD CARROT-FAMILY FORAGING

regional_scope: Minnesota / Upper Midwest (All Minnesota public parks, SNAs, forests, and prairies)
voucher_source: Bell Museum Herbarium and USDA PLANTS

poisonous_lookalike: Wild ginseng (Panax quinquefolius), native orchids (Cypripedium), wild leeks (Allium tricoccum), prairie turnip
observable_exclusions: Even on lawful private land with explicit permission, underground parts present the highest risk of confusing dormant toxic roots and concentrating soil heavy metals

regional_scope: Minnesota / Upper Midwest (Wetlands, woods, and meadows across Minnesota)
voucher_source: Bell Museum Herbarium and USDA PLANTS

poisonous_lookalike: Cicuta maculata, Conium maculatum, Anticlea/Zigadenus, Convallaria majalis, Iris versicolor, Podophyllum peltatum
observable_exclusions: Missing intact above-ground flowers/foliage, missing onion scent on bulbs, wet-ground umbels, or public-land status triggers immediate STOP

regional_scope: Minnesota / Upper Midwest (Minnesota spring hardwood forests (elms, ash, aspen, oak))

diagnostic_features: Deep regular honeycomb pits and ridges; cap fused directly to stem; 100% continuous hollow interior from tip to base on lengthwise section
poisonous_lookalike: Gyromitra esculenta / G. brunnea (lethal gyromitrin false morels — wrinkled brain-like lobes, chambered cottony interior), Verpa bohemica (thimble-like free-hanging cap, cottony stem)
observable_exclusions: Wrinkled brain lobes; chambered or cotton-stuffed interior; cap hanging free like a skirt; raw consumption causes GI/neurologic illness

regional_scope: Minnesota / Upper Midwest (Dead or living Minnesota oaks and hardwoods)
voucher_source: Bell Museum Fungarium and MyCoPortal
diagnostic_features: Bright sulfur-orange to salmon overlapping shelving brackets on hardwood trunks or oak bases; tiny bright yellow or pale-white pore underside (NO gills); white spore print
poisonous_lookalike: Laetiporus huroniensis (conifer-growing sulfur shelf linked to frequent severe GI poisoning), Hapalopilus rutilans (toxic violet-staining polypore), Omphalotus illudens (gilled jack-o-lantern)
observable_exclusions: Presence of true gills (jack-o-lantern); growth on conifers (hemlock/spruce/pine) or toxic yew/locust hosts; chalky old hard brackets

regional_scope: Minnesota / Upper Midwest (Bases of mature or dead Minnesota oak trees)
voucher_source: Bell Museum Fungarium and MyCoPortal
diagnostic_features: Dense overlapping rosette of wavy gray-brown fan-shaped fronds emerging from a branched white base at mature oaks; tiny white decurrent pore surface (NO gills); white spore print
poisonous_lookalike: Meripilus sumstinei (black-staining polypore — stains dark black when bruised), Bondarzewia berkeleyi (large thick cream lobes)
observable_exclusions: True gills; heavy black bruising on handling; growth away from oaks/hardwoods; insect-ridden or foul-smelling old clusters

regional_scope: Minnesota / Upper Midwest (Minnesota oak and mixed hardwood soil/moss)
voucher_source: Bell Museum Fungarium and MyCoPortal
diagnostic_features: Growing directly from SOIL (not clustered on wood); blunt forked shallow false gill ridges running down stem (or nearly smooth underside); solid white interior flesh peeling like string cheese; subtle fruity scent
poisonous_lookalike: Omphalotus illudens (toxic jack-o-lantern — clustered on WOOD/buried roots, sharp thin blade-like true gills, orange interior flesh, causes severe prolonged vomiting), Hygrophoropsis aurantiaca
observable_exclusions: Dense clusters on wood/stumps; sharp knife-like true gills; orange interior flesh when sliced lengthwise

regional_scope: Minnesota / Upper Midwest (Mossy Minnesota oak and mixed hardwood floors)
voucher_source: Bell Museum Fungarium and MyCoPortal

poisonous_lookalike: Turbinellus floccosus (scaly vase — larger orange-scaly funnel causing GI distress), dark gilled woodland mushrooms
observable_exclusions: True blade-like gills; bright orange scaly cap; solid stuffed stem; growth directly on rotting logs

regional_scope: Minnesota / Upper Midwest (Dead or dying Minnesota hardwoods (aspen, elm, oak, maple))
voucher_source: Bell Museum Fungarium and MyCoPortal

poisonous_lookalike: Pleurocybella porrigens (angel wing — thin fragile pure-white funnels strictly on CONIFER wood, linked to fatal encephalopathy in kidney-impaired patients), Lentinellus ursinus (acrid saw-toothed gills), Omphalotus
observable_exclusions: Growth on conifer/hemlock/spruce wood (angel wing risk); saw-toothed gill edges; rusty/brown spore print; orange flesh

regional_scope: Minnesota / Upper Midwest (Dead or wounded Minnesota hardwoods (oak, beech, maple, birch))

poisonous_lookalike: Artomyces pyxidatus (crown-tipped coral — upward-pointing tiny-crowned branches, not hanging icicles), Ramaria (some GI-toxic yellow/pink soil corals)
observable_exclusions: Upward-pointing branching corals on soil; yellowed dry sour-smelling aged specimens; protected park/SNA harvest bans

regional_scope: Minnesota / Upper Midwest (Minnesota meadows, pastures, woods)

poisonous_lookalike: Immature Amanita egg buttons (LETHAL — vertical slice reveals embryonic cap/gill/stem silhouette inside outer universal veil!), Scleroderma citrinum (toxic pigskin earthball — thick leathery rind, dark purple-black interior)
observable_exclusions: ANY faint internal outline of gills/stem (LETHAL Amanita egg!); dark purplish/yellow/olive interior (earthball or maturing puffball spores)

regional_scope: Minnesota / Upper Midwest (Disturbed lawns, gravel paths, edges across Minnesota)
voucher_source: Bell Museum Fungarium and MyCoPortal

regional_scope: Minnesota / Upper Midwest (Dead or dying Minnesota elms, maples, boxelders)
voucher_source: Bell Museum Fungarium and MyCoPortal

poisonous_lookalike: Gilled wood mushrooms, tough woody Ganoderma/Fomes brackets
observable_exclusions: True blade-like gills; missing dark velvety stem base; woody leathery mature brackets; urban sprayed trees

regional_scope: Minnesota / Upper Midwest (Living paper and yellow birch trees in northern Minnesota)
voucher_source: Bell Museum Fungarium and MyCoPortal

poisonous_lookalike: Woody tree burls (solid swirling wood grain lacking rusty cork interior), Fomes fomentarius (smooth hoof-shaped tinder conk)
observable_exclusions: Chaga contains extremely high soluble oxalates linked to documented oxalate nephropathy/kidney failure; hacking live birch trees in State/National Parks or SNAs is strictly illegal

regional_scope: Minnesota / Upper Midwest (Northern Minnesota conifer-birch and oak forests)
voucher_source: Bell Museum Fungarium and MyCoPortal
life_stage: Spongy pore tube underside & netted/scabrous stem
diagnostic_features: Fleshy cap-and-stem mushrooms bearing a spongy layer of vertical pore tubes underneath instead of gills; netted stem reticulation (Boletus) or dark scaly scabers (Leccinum)
poisonous_lookalike: Rubroboletus / Boletus huronensis / Suillellus (red- or orange-pored and rapid blue-staining boletes causing severe GI poisoning), Tylopilus felleus (pink-pored intensely bitter bolete)
observable_exclusions: Red or orange pore mouths; rapid deep navy-blue bruising on cut flesh/pores; pink pore tint; raw Leccinum causes severe GI illness

regional_scope: Minnesota / Upper Midwest (Clustered on stumps, roots, and bases of Minnesota trees)
voucher_source: Bell Museum Fungarium and MyCoPortal
life_stage: White spore print vs deadly rusty-brown Galerina
diagnostic_features: Clustered honey-yellow to brownish caps with tiny dark central hairs/scales; white-to-buff attached gills; cottony stem ring; strictly WHITE spore print on dark paper
poisonous_lookalike: Galerina marginata (DEADLY GALERINA — contains lethal amatoxins identical to death cap! Grows on deadwood in autumn, smooth brown cap, faint ring, RUSTY-BROWN spore print!), Hypholoma fasciculare (sulfur tuft — green-gray gills, purple-brown spores)
observable_exclusions: ANY rusty-brown, cinnamon, or purple-brown spore print triggers immediate lethal STOP; never mix specimens from different clusters; raw Armillaria is GI-toxic

regional_scope: Minnesota / Upper Midwest (Mossy Minnesota conifer and hardwood forest floors)
voucher_source: Bell Museum Fungarium and MyCoPortal
life_stage: Cap-and-stem with fragile pale spines beneath
diagnostic_features: Pale buff-to-apricot cap-and-stem mushroom growing on forest soil with brittle pale downward-pointing tiny teeth/spines covering the underside instead of gills or pores; white spore print
poisonous_lookalike: Sarcodon / Bankera (tough scaly dark-brown toothed fungi with brown spores), gilled orange woodland mushrooms
observable_exclusions: True gills or pores; dark scaly cap with brown spore print; woody bitter flesh

regional_scope: Minnesota / Upper Midwest (Bases of oaks and conifers in Upper Midwest woods)
voucher_source: Bell Museum Fungarium and MyCoPortal
diagnostic_features: Large brain-to-cauliflower rosette of smooth flattened cream-to-yellowish wavy ribbon lobes emerging from a central root-like base near trees; smooth spore-bearing ribbon faces; white spore print
poisonous_lookalike: Ramaria spp. (round-tipped branching coral mushrooms — several cause severe GI distress), Grifola frondosa (pored fronds)
observable_exclusions: Round cylindrical pointed coral branches (Ramaria); porous underside; heavily soiled or buggy crevices

regional_scope: Minnesota / Upper Midwest (Dead Minnesota hardwoods (elm, aspen, willow) in late fall/winter thaws)
voucher_source: Bell Museum Fungarium and MyCoPortal
life_stage: Velvety dark stem & white spores vs lethal Galerina
diagnostic_features: Small clusters on hardwood logs with sticky orange-brown caps, NO stem ring, tough dark brown-black velvety lower stem, and strictly WHITE spore print
poisonous_lookalike: Galerina marginata (DEADLY AMATOXIN — faint stem ring, pale striated stem lacking black velvet, RUSTY-BROWN spore print; can fruit late into chilly autumn on overlapping deadwood!)
observable_exclusions: Presence of a stem ring; non-velvety pale stem; ANY rusty-brown spore print triggers immediate lethal STOP

synonyms: Separating safe-morphology myths from fungal hazards
regional_scope: Minnesota / Upper Midwest (All Minnesota forest and meadow fungal habitats)
voucher_source: Bell Museum Fungarium and MyCoPortal
diagnostic_features: Reinforces that even non-gilled groups (boletes, corals, puffballs, false morels) include severe or lethal toxins—every fungal order demands multi-character verification and spore-print/cutaway checks
poisonous_lookalike: Gyromitra (false morels), Scleroderma (earthballs), Amanita egg buttons, red-pored boletes, toxic Ramaria corals, Conifer Laetiporus
observable_exclusions: Any shortcut ("no gills means safe") is dangerously false and fails immediately against Gyromitra, Amanita buttons, and red-pored boletes

synonyms: Mandatory expert verification gate for all fungi
regional_scope: Minnesota / Upper Midwest (All Minnesota macrofungi study and review workflows)
voucher_source: Bell Museum Fungarium and MyCoPortal
diagnostic_features: Requires every fungal identification candidate to pass multi-view photography, intact base inspection, spore-print deposit, substrate record, MyCoPortal voucher comparison, and independent qualified mycologist review
poisonous_lookalike: Cryptic toxic species complexes across Amanita, Galerina, Cortinarius, Lepiota, Inocybe, and Entoloma
observable_exclusions: No automated image tool, field card, or conceptual SVG diagram can clear any wild mushroom for human consumption

regional_scope: Minnesota / Upper Midwest (Minnesota oak-pine woodlands & North American parks (CDC MMWR))
voucher_source: Bell Museum Fungarium and MyCoPortal
diagnostic_features: White to greenish-olive cap; FREE white gills; white spore print; membranous skirt ring (annulus); sac-like basal cup (volva) often hidden below leaf litter
poisonous_lookalike: Agaricus meadow mushrooms, Volvariella paddy-straw mushrooms, Lycoperdon puffballs (at immature egg-button stage)
observable_exclusions: LETHAL HEAT-STABLE AMATOXINS (survive boiling/drying/freezing); delayed 6–24 hr GI onset followed by false recovery and acute fatal liver failure

regional_scope: Minnesota / Upper Midwest (Rotting hardwood and conifer logs across Minnesota)
voucher_source: Bell Museum Fungarium and MyCoPortal
diagnostic_features: Small honey-to-cinnamon brown smooth moist cap; attached tan-to-rusty gills; fragile faint stem ring; pale fibrillose stem; diagnostic RUSTY-BROWN spore print on white paper
poisonous_lookalike: Armillaria (honey mushrooms), Flammulina velutipes (winter enoki), Kuehneromyces mutabilis
observable_exclusions: CONTAINS LETHAL HEAT-STABLE AMATOXINS identical to death cap; delayed 6–24 hr GI onset preceding fatal liver/kidney failure

regional_scope: Minnesota / Upper Midwest (Minnesota sandy pine and mixed hardwood forests)
voucher_source: Bell Museum Fungarium and MyCoPortal
diagnostic_features: Reddish-brown to tan wrinkled convoluted brain-like lobed cap (lacking regular honeycomb pits); thick irregular stem with chambered/cottony stuffed interior on lengthwise slice
poisonous_lookalike: Morchella spp. (true hollow honeycomb morels)
observable_exclusions: Contains gyromitrin metabolizing into toxic monomethylhydrazine causing vomiting, hemolysis, seizures, liver injury, and death—even cooking vapors are hazardous

regional_scope: Minnesota / Upper Midwest (Northern Minnesota mossy conifer bogs and spruce woods)
voucher_source: Bell Museum Fungarium and MyCoPortal
diagnostic_features: Cinnamon-to-tawny orange-brown cap with cobweb-like filamentous veil (cortina) stretching from cap margin to stem on young specimens leaving rusty-orange spore-dusted threads; rusty-brown spore print
poisonous_lookalike: Cantharellus (chanterelles — lack cobweb veil and rusty spores), edible autumn woodland mushrooms
observable_exclusions: Contains heat-stable ORELLANINE causing silent delayed irreversible kidney failure appearing 2 to 14+ DAYS after ingestion

regional_scope: Minnesota / Upper Midwest (Clustered on dead hardwood stumps and buried oak roots in MN)
voucher_source: Bell Museum Fungarium and MyCoPortal
diagnostic_features: Bright pumpkin-orange caps growing in tight overlapping clusters directly from wood or buried roots; SHARP thin blade-like decurrent TRUE gills; orange interior flesh when sliced
poisonous_lookalike: Cantharellus (golden chanterelles — soil-dwelling, blunt forked false ridges, white interior flesh), Laetiporus (pored brackets)
observable_exclusions: Contains illudin S toxins causing severe, violent, prolonged vomiting, abdominal cramps, and diarrhea within 1–3 hours

regional_scope: Minnesota / Upper Midwest (Minnesota lawns, parks, and grassy fields after summer rain)
voucher_source: Bell Museum Fungarium and MyCoPortal
life_stage: Large scaly lawn umbrella w/ olive-green spores
diagnostic_features: Large white umbrella-shaped cap (10–30 cm) with tan-brown surface scales; ring on smooth tall stem; free gills turning dingy gray-green with age; unmistakable OLIVE-GREEN spore print on white paper
poisonous_lookalike: Macrolepiota procera (parasol — white spores, snakeskin stem), Chlorophyllum rhacodes (shaggy parasol — white spores), Agaricus (chocolate-brown spores)
observable_exclusions: Leading cause of mushroom poisonings in North America; causes severe rapid vomiting, bloody diarrhea, and dehydration

regional_scope: Minnesota / Upper Midwest (Wet ditches, marshes, stream banks, and meadows across Minnesota)
voucher_source: Bell Museum Herbarium and USDA PLANTS
diagnostic_features: Tall smooth green-to-purple-streaked hollow stems; twice-to-thrice pinnately compound toothed leaves whose side veins terminate specifically in the NOTCHES between leaf teeth; flat white compound umbels; clustered fleshy roots displaying horizontal hollow chambers when sliced
poisonous_lookalike: Wild carrot (Daucus), wild parsnip, wild angelica, elderberry (woody), cattail/wetland mint co-occurrence
observable_exclusions: Contains CICUTOXIN—a violently potent convulsant neurotoxin causing rapid uncontrollable seizures, respiratory arrest, and death within hours from a tiny bite of root or stem

regional_scope: Minnesota / Upper Midwest (Roadsides, ditches, stream edges, disturbed meadows in MN)
voucher_source: Bell Museum Herbarium and USDA PLANTS
diagnostic_features: Tall (1–3 m) completely HAIRLESS hollow stems unmistakably blotched with purple-red spots; finely divided fern-like lacy leaves with musty mousy odor; flat white compound umbel clusters; white parsnip-like taproot
poisonous_lookalike: Daucus carota (hairy green stem), Pastinaca sativa, wild chervil/parsley
observable_exclusions: Contains lethal CONIINE alkaloids causing ascending neuromuscular paralysis and fatal respiratory failure; sap also irritates skin/eyes

regional_scope: Minnesota / Upper Midwest (Woodland edges, fencerows, disturbed ground across Minnesota)
voucher_source: Bell Museum Herbarium and USDA PLANTS
diagnostic_features: Woody climbing vine with lobed leaves, purple swept-back star flowers with bright yellow central cone, and shiny oval red berries (S. dulcamara) OR herbaceous stems with white star flowers and glossy green/black berries (S. ptycanthum)
poisonous_lookalike: Wild rose hips, wild currants, blueberries, lambsquarters
observable_exclusions: Contains toxic glycoalkaloids (solanine, dulcamarine) especially concentrated in unripe berries and foliage, causing GI, neurologic, and pediatric poisoning

regional_scope: Minnesota / Upper Midwest (Minnesota shaded woodlands, edges, and clearings)
voucher_source: Bell Museum Herbarium and USDA PLANTS
life_stage: White woodland flat heads / purple berry racemes
diagnostic_features: White snakeroot: opposite toothed 3-veined leaves on smooth stems topped with snowy-white fuzzy flower heads (contains tremetol—cause of historic milk sickness). Pokeweed: tall smooth reddish-purple stems with large smooth-edged leaves and hanging grapelike strings of glossy ink-purple berries
poisonous_lookalike: Stinging nettle (lacks white flat heads), elderberry (woody opposite compound shrub), wild grapes
observable_exclusions: ALL parts of white snakeroot contain tremetol; ALL parts of pokeweed (especially roots, purple stems, and seeds/berries) contain toxic phytolaccatoxins and mitogens causing severe GI and cardiac toxicity

regional_scope: Minnesota / Upper Midwest (Minnesota woodlands, parks, edges, and thickets)
voucher_source: Bell Museum Herbarium and USDA PLANTS
life_stage: Sub-opposite leaves, twig spine & black fruit
diagnostic_features: Invasive shrub/small tree with mostly SUB-OPPOSITE glossy dark-green finely toothed leaves showing curved veins, short sharp thorn-like tip nestled between paired terminal buds, orange inner bark, and tight clusters of pea-sized black 3–4 seeded berries
poisonous_lookalike: Chokecherry (Prunus), serviceberry (Amelanchier), elderberry (Sambucus), black chokeberry (Aronia)
observable_exclusions: Contains anthraquinone glycosides causing violent diarrhea, cramping, and dehydration; stays green late into November after native shrubs drop leaves

regional_scope: Minnesota / Upper Midwest (Minnesota river floodplains and moist wooded thickets)
voucher_source: Bell Museum Herbarium and USDA PLANTS
diagnostic_features: Woody twining vine completely LACKING tendrils; smooth-edged shallowly 3–7 lobed leaves with petiole attached slightly inside the leaf blade edge; clusters of dusty blue-black grape-like fruit each containing ONE flat crescent-moon-shaped ridged pit
poisonous_lookalike: Vitis riparia (wild riverbank grape — forked tendrils, coarsely toothed leaves, 2–4 smooth pear-shaped seeds)
observable_exclusions: Contains lethal isoquinoline alkaloids (dauricine) causing paralysis, convulsions, and cardiac arrest—even a few berries can fatally poison a child

regional_scope: Minnesota / Upper Midwest (Rich shaded Minnesota deciduous and mixed forests)
voucher_source: Bell Museum Herbarium and USDA PLANTS
life_stage: Compound jagged leaves & glossy stalked berries
diagnostic_features: Bushy herbaceous perennial with large twice-or-thrice compound sharply jagged leaflets; thick red stalks holding porcelain-white black-dotted berries (doll-eyes, A. pachypoda) or slender stalks holding glossy cherry-red berries (A. rubra)
poisonous_lookalike: Cornus canadensis (bunchberry), Ribes, Viburnum, Gaultheria
observable_exclusions: Contains cardiogenic glycosides and protoanemonin-like toxins causing immediate oral blistering, gastroenteritis, dizziness, and potentially fatal cardiac arrest

regional_scope: Minnesota / Upper Midwest (Northern Minnesota shaded forests and widespread urban landscaping)
voucher_source: Bell Museum Herbarium and USDA PLANTS
life_stage: Flat dark 2-ranked needles & red fleshy cup
diagnostic_features: Low sprawling evergreen shrub (wild) or trimmed hedge (landscaped) with flat pointed dark-green single needles arranged in two flat rows on green twigs and open fleshy scarlet-red cup-like arils surrounding a dark olive-black seed
poisonous_lookalike: Pinus strobus (5-needle bundles), Abies balsamea (white underside stripes, upright dry cones), Picea (4-sided pegged needles)
observable_exclusions: ALL needles, bark, twigs, and seeds contain lethal TAXINE cardiac alkaloids causing sudden fatal cardiac arrhythmias and arrest with minimal warning

accepted_binomial: Toxicodendron radicans / T. rydbergii / T. vernix
regional_scope: Minnesota / Upper Midwest (Minnesota woodlands, trails, dunes (ivy) and wet bogs (sumac))
voucher_source: Bell Museum Herbarium and USDA PLANTS
diagnostic_features: Poison ivy: strictly ALTERNATE three-leaflet compound leaves (central leaflet on longer stalk), smooth/notched/lobed edges, fuzzy rope-like climbing vines or low woody shrub, waxy white berries. Poison sumac: wet bogs, 7–13 smooth-edged leaflets, drooping white berries
poisonous_lookalike: Parthenocissus (Virginia creeper — 5 leaflets), Rubus (thorny canes), Rhus typhina (upland fuzzy red berry cones)
observable_exclusions: Urushiol oil persists for years on clothes, boots, pet fur, and dead winter stems; BURNING poison ivy/sumac vaporizes urushiol causing life-threatening lung airway inflammation

regional_scope: Minnesota / Upper Midwest (Sunny roadsides, prairies, trail edges across Minnesota)
voucher_source: Bell Museum Herbarium and USDA PLANTS
life_stage: Grooved stem, pinnate toothed leaves & yellow umbels
diagnostic_features: Stout grooved hollow stems with alternate pinnately compound coarsely toothed leaves and broad flat-topped YELLOW compound umbels; sap contains furocoumarins
poisonous_lookalike: Golden Alexanders (Zizia aurea — smaller, finer leaflets), Heracleum maximum (cow parsnip — giant white umbels, also phototoxic), Heracleum mantegazzianum (giant hogweed)
observable_exclusions: Sap contact followed by sunlight (UV) causes severe painful second-degree chemical burns, blistering, and months-long skin discoloration—even through thin brushed weeds

regional_scope: Minnesota / Upper Midwest (Shaded yards, naturalized woods, wet seeps)
voucher_source: Bell Museum Herbarium and USDA PLANTS
life_stage: Broad parallel-veined spring leaves (NO onion scent)
diagnostic_features: Lily-of-the-valley: paired smooth parallel-veined lance leaves lacking onion odor, arching stems of fragrant white hanging bells, and red-orange autumn berries. False hellebore: pleated broad ribbed clasping leaves in wet woods
poisonous_lookalike: Allium tricoccum (wild leek/ramps — unmistakable strong onion odor on leaf and bulb)
observable_exclusions: Convallaria contains lethal cardiac glycosides (convallatoxin); Veratrum contains lethal steroidal alkaloids causing severe bradycardia, hypotension, and death
